title: Direct Action Day and the Calcutta riots
summary: The All-India Muslim League called 16 August 1946 as Direct Action Day to press its demand for Pakistan. In Calcutta, then ruled by a League ministry, the day turned into several days of communal violence between Hindus and Muslims. The official estimate was 4,000 dead; other estimates reach 10,000. The riots fed later violence elsewhere in India.

uncertainty.note: Sciences Po dates the riots 16–19 August 1946; Banglapedia says Calcutta was largely calm by 22 August.

as_recorded.value: 16 August 1946, the day the Muslim League had designated as "Direct Action Day"

importance.justification: Among the deadliest outbreaks of communal violence before Partition and a turning point in the path to it.

audience_note: Describes mass communal killing of civilians. Death toll and the share of blame are disputed between Congress, Muslim League and British accounts.

sources.title: The Calcutta Riots of 1946
sources.publisher: Sciences Po (Mass Violence and Resistance Online Encyclopedia)

reviewer_note: Deaths given as attributed figures: 4,000 dead and 100,000 injured as the official estimate (Banglapedia, not independently verified); 5,000 to 10,000 dead and about 15,000 wounded (Sciences Po, noting that no precise figures exist). Blame is contested and the summary does not assign it. Pin is the city centre; the worst-hit area is a district of north Calcutta.
